clue.text: Booker? With prize ultimately secured, trim one's sails

indicators.note: secured means the letter is held fast inside the other word

parts.note: a referee books players, so a Booker is a REF

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of prize is used

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: A literary prize-winner, having secured the award, decides to take things more cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Booker as a cryptic description (one who books, a referee) rather than the literary prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To reef is to roll up part of a sail to reduce its area in strong wind.

clue.text: Power of the mind seen in part of 24 across

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
inner, as in one's inner thoughts, means of the mind

explanation.surface: Mental strength is on show in a corner of suburban London.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is METROLAND, the London suburbs served by the Metropolitan line; Pinner is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London lying within the area once marketed as Metroland.

clue.text: If pedant is confused about hard recipe initially, he seeks way to proceed

indicators.note: is confused tells us the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of recipe

parts.note: its first letter is R

explanation.surface: A muddled pedant, faced with a tricky recipe, looks for some way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word here: IF PEDANT plus H are rearranged to PATHFINDE, and the R from recipe follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathfinder is a scout or pioneer who finds a route for others to follow.

clue.text: One of six in charge of our land, one a so-called farmer

definitions.text: One of six in charge of our land
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Britain has had six kings of this name
second meaning: King ... III was nicknamed Farmer ... for his interest in agriculture

explanation.walkthrough: Six British kings were called George; George III earned the nickname Farmer George for his love of farming.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was borne by six British monarchs, one of them known affectionately by a rural nickname.

clue.text: Restrained, cut line in second edition

indicators.note: in means the cut and the line are placed inside the other letters

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: An editor, held back, trims a line from a book's second edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackled means bound in chains or fetters, hence held back or constrained.

clue.text: See 7
Imaginary character, one of the first two Wells wrote about

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the face people fancy they see on the lunar surface

definitions.text: one of the first two Wells wrote about
definitions.meaning: second meaning: H G Wells wrote The First Men in the ..., about two men who travel there

explanation.walkthrough: In The First Men in the Moon by H G Wells, Bedford and Cavor are the first two to reach the Moon, so either is a man there.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure is a folklore face seen in the lunar markings, and also any man literally on the Moon.

clue.text: Part of painter's work starts off collection of art treasures

indicators.note: starts off means we take the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A painter's work forms the beginning of a gallery's collection of treasures.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter applies paint in layers, each layer being one coat of the job.

clue.text: Hungarian saint containing the blaze I mishandled

indicators.note: mishandled tells us the letters of these words are handled clumsily and jumbled

explanation.surface: A saint's relic is found containing evidence of a fire badly managed.
explanation.definitionFit: St Elizabeth of Hungary was a thirteenth-century princess canonised for her charity.

clue.text: Love label linked with old wine-producing region

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A fond label is attached to bottles from an old vineyard area.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island known for its Pinot Noir vineyards.

clue.text: Bird presented in last part of French chapter

parts.note: fin is the French word for end, the last part

explanation.surface: A bird appears near the end of a French book's chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last part of French' looks like a letter pick, but it is the French word for 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The finch is a small seed-eating songbird, such as the goldfinch or chaffinch.

clue.text: With repetition of first part, contrive changes to sentence again

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into a fresh order

parts.note: the first letter of contrive, C, is used a second time

explanation.surface: A legal drafter repeats a phrase, contriving to amend a sentence once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is CONTRIVE plus a second copy of its first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvict is to find someone guilty once more, so to pass sentence again.

clue.text: Large rodent, hard to handle, not keeping up like pig

indicators.note: not keeping means the word up is dropped from the rodent

parts.note: the porcupine is a large rodent whose quills make it hard to pick up

explanation.surface: A prickly large rodent that won't keep up is compared to a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcine is the adjective for pigs, from Latin porcus, meaning swinish or hog-like.

clue.text: Beat seed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rhythmic throb, as of the heart
second meaning: the edible seed of a legume, such as a lentil

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests beating seed, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a heartbeat felt at the wrist and edible legume seeds like peas and lentils.

clue.text: Found pound and ounce, say, in abbreviated dictionary

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

indicators.note: in means the cat is placed inside the dictionary's initials

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary's initials, its usual short form
the ounce, or snow leopard, is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A pound and an ounce turn up listed in a shortened dictionary of weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ounce' pretends to be a weight beside 'pound'; here it is the snow leopard, a cat. 'abbreviated' tells you to use the dictionary's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Located, as a past tense verb, means found or tracked down, as in locating a missing item.

clue.text: Novel form in old verse penned by Conservatives

indicators.note: penned by means the verse is enclosed by the Conservatives' letters

parts.note: two names for Conservatives: C, the abbreviation, and TORY
rimes is an old spelling of rhymes, verse

explanation.surface: A type of novel written in old-fashioned verse by Conservative politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime story, or detective fiction, is a genre of novel built around a crime and its solving.

clue.text: Letters from London nearly delivered for poet

indicators.note: Letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow
delivered adds that the words given hand over these letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mail from London, almost delivered, is addressed to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'delivered for poet' as the definition; 'delivered' instead joins 'Letters from' in signalling the hidden run, and 'poet' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a Jacobean metaphysical poet and Dean of St Paul's in London.

clue.text: Endless fortune I had put together, that's clear

indicators.note: Endless means the last letter of luck is cut off

parts.note: luck is fortune
I had contracts to I'd, giving ID

explanation.surface: Someone sums up: with endless good fortune they had, all was plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear and easy to understand, as in a lucid explanation.

clue.text: Coping partly with limited capital, just under fifteen pounds

parts.note: cap is the clipped form of capital, as in caps for capital letters
a stone is fourteen pounds, just under fifteen

explanation.surface: Someone is coping, barely, on limited funds of almost fifteen pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coping' looks like managing, but it is the top course of a wall; a stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is one of the stones forming the protective top course, or coping, of a wall.

clue.text: Like the Chairman's little work (or books in general, we hear)

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the past participle of the verb for taking in books, as in being well versed in books generally

explanation.surface: A puzzle about Chairman Mao's little book, or reading matter generally.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chairman is Mao, whose quotations formed the Little Red Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Zedong's Quotations was popularly known in the West as the Little Red Book from its cover colour.

clue.text: Deity repeatedly upset another — that's very unusual

indicators.note: repeatedly means the god's name is given a second time in a row

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: Siva, or Shiva, is another deity, the Hindu god

explanation.surface: A god keeps upsetting another god, which is quite out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Rara avis is Latin for rare bird, used of a person or thing seldom met with.

clue.text: Don't allow to leave with odd characters out of discretion

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters of discretion leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: Discretion bars odd characters from leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice in is said of a ship trapped in frozen water, unable to leave port.
explanation.definitionFit: When a vessel is iced in, frozen water holds it fast so it cannot depart.

clue.text: Agent in European capital backed Julian, say

indicators.note: backed means the whole is read from back to front
in means the agent sits inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep, or representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: An agent in Rome supported someone called Julian.
explanation.walkthrough: Julian is the Roman emperor Julian the Apostate, not a modern name.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian ruled the Roman Empire from 361 to 363, an example of a supreme imperial ruler.

clue.text: Increase organised valet parking in large parts of East End

indicators.note: parking in means the rearranged letters are put inside the pair
the capital, or large, letters of East and End are their initial Es
organised means the letters of valet are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Valet parking has been organised to boost trade in much of London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'valet parking' reads as one phrase, but 'parking in' is the insertion signal; the East End is a working-class district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise or lift something higher, so to increase its level.

clue.text: Denouement that's heart-rending? Not half

indicators.note: Not half means the first half of the twelve letters is dropped, keeping the back half

explanation.surface: A climax to a story that is only half as moving as hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A denouement is the final resolution of a plot, the way a story is brought to a close.

clue.text: King or president

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the legendary King ... of Camelot
second meaning: Chester A ..., 21st president of the United States

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the Round Table monarch of legend and to a nineteenth-century American head of state.

clue.text: Encountered Oliver's friend in London suburban area

parts.note: met means encountered
Roland and Oliver were the inseparable paladins of Charlemagne

explanation.surface: Someone met Oliver's pal out in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver is not Dickens's Twist but the companion of Roland in the Song of Roland.
explanation.definitionFit: Metroland was the name for the suburbs north-west of London built along the Metropolitan Railway.

clue.text: Source of inspiration and great power in the writer

indicators.note: in means the power goes inside the writer

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so me
the US is a great power among nations

explanation.surface: A writer feels a great power within that inspires the work.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Muses were goddesses who inspired artists, so any inspiring figure is one.

clue.text: Old author I'd pronounced woke?

parts.note: to pen is to author, and the pen stands for the writer

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: I'd, said aloud, is the same as eyed

explanation.surface: An elderly author announces that they have woken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woke' is used in its modern sense of alert to injustice, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-eyed means watchful and fully aware, close to the slang sense of being alert to social issues.

clue.text: It's put in the kind of barns churches once found helpful

definitions.text: kind of barns churches once found helpful

indicators.note: put in means it goes inside the word the

parts.note: It's means it is, so the word it

explanation.surface: Something is stored in the sort of barn the old church found useful.
explanation.walkthrough: Tithe barns held the tenth of produce owed to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of farm produce paid to the church, stored in large tithe barns.

clue.text: See 25
Become aware of things smelt, heard but not seen

indicators.note: heard but not seen means the word is taken by its sound alone, not its spelling

parts.note: scents are things smelt

explanation.surface: Noticing smells and sounds of something invisible.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to perceive or detect it, to grow conscious of it.

clue.text: Part of bicycle that doesn't make it to 24 across?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the inflatable rubber tube inside a tyre

definitions.text: that doesn't make it to 24 across
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an inner London Underground line, which stops short of the Metroland suburbs

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground; an inner line serves central London and never reaches the outer suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable inside a cycle tyre, and also a jokey name for a central London Underground train.
